title.zh: 卷424 列傳二百十一 吴振棫 张亮基 毛鸿宾 张凯嵩
title.en: Volume 424 Biographies 211: Wu Zhenyu, Zhang Liangji, Mao Hongbin, Zhang Kaisong
title.raw: 卷424 列傳二百十一 吴振棫 张亮基 毛鸿宾 张凯嵩

sentences.zh: =吳振棫=吳振棫，字仲雲，浙江錢塘人。

translations.literal: Wu Zhenyu, style name Zhongyun, was a native of Qiantang in Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Zhenyu, whose style was Zhongyun, came from Qiantang in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶十九年進士，選庶吉士，授編修。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year of the Jiaqing reign he passed the jinshi examination, was selected as a bachelor in the Hanlin Academy, and was appointed reviser.
translations.idiomatic: He became a jinshi in Jiaqing 19, entered the Hanlin as a bachelor, and received appointment as reviser.

sentences.zh: 道光二年，出為雲南大理知府，歷山東登州、沂州、濟南，安徽鳳陽知府；

translations.literal: In the second year of the Daoguang reign he went out as prefect of Dali in Yunnan, and successively served as prefect of Dengzhou, Yizhou, and Jinan in Shandong and of Fengyang in Anhui;
translations.idiomatic: In Daoguang 2 he was posted as prefect of Dali in Yunnan, then held successive prefectures in Shandong—Dengzhou, Yizhou, and Jinan—and Fengyang in Anhui;

sentences.zh: 山東登萊青道；

translations.literal: the Shandong Deng-Lai-Qing Circuit intendant;
translations.idiomatic: the Shandong Deng-Lai-Qing circuit intendant;

sentences.zh: 貴州糧儲道；

translations.literal: the Guizhou grain and storage intendant;
translations.idiomatic: the Guizhou grain and storage intendant;

sentences.zh: 貴州按察使；

translations.literal: the Guizhou provincial judicial commissioner;
translations.idiomatic: the Guizhou provincial judicial commissioner;

sentences.zh: 山西、四川布政使。

translations.literal: and provincial administration commissioner of Shanxi and Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: and provincial administration commissioner in Shanxi and Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 咸豐二年，擢雲南巡撫。

translations.literal: In the second year of the Xianfeng reign he was promoted to governor of Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: In Xianfeng 2 he was elevated to governor of Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 尋甸、東川回匪蠢動，粵匪由廣西闌入開化、廣南境，偕總督吳文鎔先後遣將擊平之。

translations.literal: Hui bandits stirred in Xundian and Dongchuan, and Cantonese rebels from Guangxi broke into the borders of Kaihua and Guangnan; together with Governor-General Wu Wenrong he successively sent generals to attack and pacify them.
translations.idiomatic: When Hui rebels rose in Xundian and Dongchuan and Cantonese rebels from Guangxi crossed into Kaihua and Guangnan, he and Governor-General Wu Wenrong dispatched troops in turn until both threats were suppressed.

sentences.zh: 四年，調陝西巡撫，未行，署雲貴總督。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was transferred to governor of Shaanxi; before he took up the post he acted as governor-general of Yunnan and Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In year 4 he was shifted to Shaanxi governor but had not yet departed when he was ordered to act as Yunnan-Guizhou governor-general.

sentences.zh: 貴州興義、普安匪起，檄安義鎮總兵金剛保等剿之。

translations.literal: Bandits rose in Xingyi and Pu'an in Guizhou, and he issued orders to Anyi garrison commander Jin Gangbao and others to suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels broke out in Guizhou's Xingyi and Pu'an, and he ordered Anyi garrison commander Jin Gangbao and others against them.

sentences.zh: 遵義亦被匪圍，合滇、黔兵力，迭戰獲勝，擒匪首楊鳳先於石阡葛莊司。

translations.literal: Zunyi was also besieged by bandits; combining Yunnan and Guizhou forces, he won repeated victories in battle and captured the bandit leader Yang Fengxian at Gezhuang Subprefecture in Shiqian.
translations.idiomatic: Zunyi too came under siege; pooling Yunnan and Guizhou troops he won successive engagements and took the rebel chief Yang Fengxian at Gezhuang in Shiqian.

sentences.zh: 五年秋，始抵陝西任。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the fifth year he finally reached Shaanxi to take office.
translations.idiomatic: Not until autumn of year 5 did he arrive in Shaanxi to assume his post.

sentences.zh: 匪首陳通明受粵匪指揮，於潼關糾眾謀響應，以計擒之，並獲其黨張順、羅吉祥等置諸法，被詔嘉獎。

translations.literal: The bandit leader Chen Tongming, acting under Cantonese rebel direction, gathered men at Tong Pass to plot a response; by stratagem he was captured, and his followers Zhang Shun, Luo Jixiang, and others were seized and punished by law, for which an imperial edict praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Rebel chief Chen Tongming, directed by Cantonese rebels, mustered men at Tong Pass to coordinate an uprising; Wu captured him by ruse, seized accomplices Zhang Shun and Luo Jixiang, and had them executed—earning an imperial commendation.

sentences.zh: 鹽課攤歸地丁，數倍於昔，奏請改行招販，先課后鹽，民便之。

translations.literal: The salt levy had been folded into the land tax and was several times what it had been; he memorialized to change to a merchant-recruitment system with tax before salt, to the people's convenience.
translations.idiomatic: With the salt tax merged into the land tax at several times the old rate, he petitioned to revert to licensed merchants and tax-before-salt, which eased the burden on the people.

sentences.zh: 未幾，擢四川總督。

translations.literal: Before long he was promoted to governor-general of Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after he was promoted to governor-general of Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 七年，調雲貴總督。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was transferred to governor-general of Yunnan and Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In year 7 he was transferred to the Yunnan-Guizhou governor-generalship.

sentences.zh: 雲南漢、回積仇，自中原兵事亟，協餉不至，回亂愈恣。

translations.literal: Han and Hui in Yunnan bore long-standing mutual hatred; as warfare in the central plains grew urgent, cooperative funds ceased to arrive, and Hui unrest grew more rampant.
translations.idiomatic: Deep Han-Hui animosity in Yunnan worsened as central-plain wars drained resources—subsidies stopped coming and Hui rebellion spread.

sentences.zh: 團練跋扈，動相殺掠，省城戒嚴。

translations.literal: Militia corps were overbearing and constantly killed and plundered one another; the provincial capital was placed under martial alert.
translations.idiomatic: Local militia ran wild, raiding one another until the capital was put on strict guard.

sentences.zh: 前任總督恆春不能制，夫婦同縊，巡撫舒興阿亦以病求去，惟布政使桑春榮困守危城。

translations.literal: The previous governor-general Hengchun could not control them; husband and wife hanged themselves together; Governor Shuxing'a also sought leave on grounds of illness; only Provincial Administration Commissioner Sang Chunrong remained trapped defending the endangered city.
translations.idiomatic: His predecessor Hengchun failed to restore order and he and his wife hanged themselves; Governor Shuxing'a pleaded illness to leave; only Sang Chunrong, as administration commissioner, held the besieged city.

sentences.zh: 文宗知振棫熟悉滇省情形，故以代之。

translations.literal: The Wenzong Emperor knew that Zhenyu was familiar with conditions in Yunnan, and therefore replaced him with him.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wenzong knew Zhenyu understood Yunnan and sent him to replace Hengchun.

sentences.zh: 命選川兵三千，攜餉五萬馳往，調前山東巡撫張亮基幫辦軍務以副之。

translations.literal: He was ordered to select three thousand Sichuan troops, carry fifty thousand taels of funds, and hurry there; the former Shandong governor Zhang Liangji was transferred to assist in military affairs as his deputy.
translations.idiomatic: He was to take three thousand Sichuan soldiers and fifty thousand taels in silver, while former Shandong governor Zhang Liangji was assigned to help manage military affairs.

sentences.zh: 振或至，先駐宣威，進次​​曲靖。

translations.literal: When Zhenyu arrived he first encamped at Xuanwei and then advanced to Qujing.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenyu reached Yunnan, halted first at Xuanwei, then moved forward to Qujing.

sentences.zh: 疏言：「先剿後撫，勢順而易，不待智者而知。

translations.literal: In a memorial he said: 'To suppress first and pacify afterward is the course that follows the trend and is easy; this is known even without a wise man.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized: 'Suppress first, pacify after—that is the easy, natural course, obvious to any thoughtful observer.

sentences.zh: 兵盛餉足，必應如是。

translations.literal: With abundant troops and ample funds, one must act accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: Only where troops are plentiful and funds secure can that policy succeed.

sentences.zh: 前督臣林則徐剿永昌回匪，兵、練萬餘，本省有餉可籌；

translations.literal: The former governor Lin Zexu suppressed Hui bandits in Yongchang with more than ten thousand soldiers and militia, and the province had funds that could be raised;
translations.idiomatic: Former governor Lin Zexu had crushed Yongchang Hui rebels with over ten thousand troops and militia, with provincial revenue to sustain them;

sentences.zh: 彌渡獲勝，匪旋受撫，其地祗迤西一隅中之一隅。

translations.literal: after victory at Midu the bandits soon submitted to pacification, and that territory was only one corner within one corner of the western circuit.
translations.idiomatic: victory at Midu led quickly to submission, and the trouble lay in but a single corner of the western frontier.

sentences.zh: 此次匪遍三迤，情形迥不相同，非數千之兵、十數万之餉所能蕆事。

translations.literal: This time bandits spread through all three western circuits; the situation is utterly different, and several thousand troops and one or two hundred thousand in funds cannot bring the matter to completion.
translations.idiomatic: Now rebels held all three western circuits—a far graver case that thousands of men and hundreds of thousands in silver could not settle.

sentences.zh: 如率意迳行，徒損國威，於事無補。

translations.literal: If one rashly proceeds straight ahead, one will only damage national prestige without helping the affair.
translations.idiomatic: To rush ahead heedlessly would only humiliate the state and achieve nothing.

sentences.zh: 臣初到滇，於漢、回兩無嫌怨，惟憑藉兵威，結以恩信，有所申訴，處以公平。

translations.literal: When I first reached Yunnan I had no grudge against either Han or Hui; I rely only on military prestige, bind them with grace and trust, and wherever there are petitions I treat them with fairness.
translations.idiomatic: On arriving I owed neither Han nor Hui a grudge; I would rely on disciplined force, win trust through fairness, and judge every grievance impartially.

sentences.zh: 省城為根本重地，省回解散，此外漸次籌辦，其負嵎抗拒者，仍當力剿。

translations.literal: The provincial capital is the fundamental vital place; disperse the Hui of the province, and beyond that proceed step by step; those who resist stubbornly should still be vigorously suppressed.
translations.idiomatic: The capital is the root: disband provincial Hui forces there, then work outward; die-hards must still be fought.

sentences.zh: 匪勢漸孤，較易得手。

translations.literal: As the bandits' strength gradually becomes isolated, it will be easier to gain success.
translations.idiomatic: Isolated rebels would be easier to defeat.

sentences.zh: 否則不自量度而急乘之，更無轉圜地步，禍更烈矣。

translations.literal: Otherwise, without measuring one's strength and pressing the attack in haste, there will be no room to turn back, and the calamity will be fiercer still.
translations.idiomatic: But overreach without means to retreat, and disaster would only deepen.

sentences.zh: 現在兵無可調，餉無可籌，宵旰焦勞，事非一省。

translations.literal: At present troops cannot be mobilized and funds cannot be raised; the emperor toils anxiously day and night, and the matter is not for one province alone.
translations.idiomatic: Today neither troops nor money can be found; the throne labors over crises nationwide, not Yunnan alone.

sentences.zh: 臣為雲南一省計，並當為天下全局計，豈容再有貽誤，致令徵調無休？

translations.literal: I plan for Yunnan as one province and must also plan for the overall situation of the empire; how can there be further delay causing endless levies of troops?
translations.idiomatic: I must weigh Yunnan against the empire—how can we afford another misstep that would trigger endless mobilizations?

sentences.zh: 故未言剿先言撫，有萬不得已之苦衷，雖成敗利鈍難以逆料，捨此亦別無良策也。

translations.literal: Therefore before speaking of suppression I speak of pacification; there is the bitter necessity of having no alternative; though success or failure and gain or loss are hard to foresee in advance, apart from this there is no other good policy.
translations.idiomatic: Hence I speak of pacification before suppression—not from choice but necessity; the outcome is uncertain, yet no better course exists.'

sentences.zh: 又奏：「在籍侍郎黃琮、御史竇墉、總兵周鳳岐奉命團練，設總局於省城。

translations.literal: He also memorialized: 'The retired grand secretary Huang Cong, Censor Dou Yong, and Regional Commander Zhou Fengqi were ordered to organize militia and established a general bureau in the provincial capital.
translations.idiomatic: He added: 'Retired Grand Secretary Huang Cong, Censor Dou Yong, and Regional Commander Zhou Fengqi were charged with militia training and set up a headquarters in the capital.

sentences.zh: 周鳳岐意見不合，引嫌不肯與聞。

translations.literal: Zhou Fengqi's views did not agree; citing scruple he refused to participate.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Fengqi, disagreeing, withdrew on grounds of conflict.

sentences.zh: 黃琮、竇墉聯銜出示，專主痛剿，民間紛紛集練，回眾疑忌日深。

translations.literal: Huang Cong and Dou Yong jointly issued proclamations insisting on stern suppression; the people rushed to form militia in confusion, and Hui suspicions deepened daily.
translations.idiomatic: Huang and Dou issued joint notices demanding harsh suppression; civilians rushed to drill while Hui distrust deepened daily.

sentences.zh: 地方官苦心解散，漢民往往閧堂塞署，逼官殺回。

translations.literal: Local officials labored to disband them, but Han people often stormed halls and blocked yamens, forcing officials to kill Hui.
translations.idiomatic: Officials struggled to disband units, yet Han mobs stormed government offices demanding executions of Hui.

sentences.zh: 故團練在他省為要務，在滇省竟為大患。

translations.literal: Therefore militia training, though essential in other provinces, in Yunnan became a great calamity.
translations.idiomatic: Thus what was vital elsewhere became Yunnan's gravest plague.

sentences.zh: 黃琮等每言省團可得六十萬人，無虞寇警。

translations.literal: Huang Cong and others constantly said the provincial militia could muster six hundred thousand men and there was no worry about bandit alarm.
translations.idiomatic: They claimed six hundred thousand provincial militiamen could hold off any foe.

sentences.zh: 回匪初至城外，不及千人，團丁招之不來，來即奔潰。

translations.literal: When Hui bandits first reached outside the walls there were fewer than a thousand; militiamen summoned would not come, and when they came they fled and collapsed at once.
translations.idiomatic: When fewer than a thousand Hui rebels first appeared outside the walls, summoned militia either failed to show or broke and ran.

sentences.zh: 近日省練一萬餘人，月需餉數万，經費不敷。

translations.literal: Recently more than ten thousand provincial militia require tens of thousands in monthly pay, and funds do not suffice.
translations.idiomatic: Over ten thousand capital militia now cost tens of thousands monthly—funds cannot cover it.

sentences.zh: 練頭自行管帶，不盡官派。

translations.literal: Militia leaders command their own bands and are not wholly under official assignment.
translations.idiomatic: Captains lead private bands beyond full official control.

sentences.zh: 回眾有求撫之意，梗議者忽用練往剿，妄殺邀功，致可撫者終不能撫。

translations.literal: The Hui masses had a mind to seek pacification, but obstructionists suddenly used militia to go suppress them, killing recklessly to claim merit, so that those who could have been pacified in the end could not be pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Hui willing to submit were attacked by militia seeking glory, so pacification never took hold.

sentences.zh: 黃琮、竇墉系特派人員，非臣力所能製，請旨定奪。

translations.literal: Huang Cong and Dou Yong are specially dispatched personnel, not within my power to restrain; I beg the imperial decision.
translations.idiomatic: Huang and Dou were imperial appointees beyond my authority—I beg the throne to decide.'

sentences.zh: 臣已諮桑春榮嚴覈守城之練，裁汰冗濫，以節糜費。

translations.literal: I have already consulted Sang Chunrong to strictly verify the militia defending the city, cut redundant numbers, and save wasteful expense.
translations.idiomatic: I have instructed Sang Chunrong to audit capital garrison militia, cut waste, and save funds.

sentences.zh: 練歸官統，如不奉調派，自行出隊，即按軍法從事，庶一事權而免掣肘。

translations.literal: Militia return to official command; if they do not obey transfer orders and go out on their own, they are dealt with by military law, so that authority may be unified and hindrance avoided.
translations.idiomatic: Militia must answer to official command; unauthorized sorties will face military justice so authority stays unified.'

sentences.zh: 」疏入，詔褫黃琮、竇墉職，許回民悔悟自新，其負固不服者，痛加剿辦。

translations.literal: ' When the memorial entered, an edict stripped Huang Cong and Dou Yong of office, permitted Hui people to repent and renew themselves, and those stubbornly defiant were to be sternly suppressed.
translations.idiomatic: The throne stripped Huang and Dou, allowed repentant Hui to reform, and ordered harsh action against die-hards.

sentences.zh: 漢民借團練為名肆行殺掠者，以軍法從事。

translations.literal: Han people who under the name of militia training carried out killing and plundering were dealt with by military law.
translations.idiomatic: Han who used militia as cover for murder and looting faced military law.

sentences.zh: 於是振棫遣漢、回委員赴省城曉諭漢、回，解釋猜嫌，分畫所居街道，撥抵難民遺產，議定章程，遣散歸業。

translations.literal: Thereupon Zhenyu sent Han and Hui commissioners to the provincial capital to instruct Han and Hui, explain away suspicions, divide the streets where they dwelt, allocate refugees' inherited property, fix regulations, and disperse them to return to their occupations.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenyu then sent Han and Hui commissioners to the capital to explain grievances, demarcate quarters, settle refugee estates, set rules, and send people home.

sentences.zh: 先後剿平霑益回匪，殲咸寧土匪李廣沅。

translations.literal: He successively suppressed Hui bandits in Zhanyi and destroyed the bandit Li Guangyuan of Xianning.
translations.idiomatic: He suppressed Zhanyi Hui rebels and destroyed Xianning bandit Li Guangyuan.

sentences.zh: 八年四月，撫局粗定，入駐省城，偕張亮基籌辦迤西剿撫事宜。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the eighth year the pacification situation was roughly settled; he entered and garrisoned the provincial capital and together with Zhang Liangji planned western-circuit suppression and pacification.
translations.idiomatic: By the fourth month of year 8 pacification was roughly in place; he entered the capital with Zhang Liangji to manage western campaigns.

sentences.zh: 臨安回匪攻府城，遣兵擊走之，又敗之於阿迷州，解河西縣之圍。

translations.literal: Hui bandits in Lin'an attacked the prefectural city; he sent troops to drive them off, again defeated them at Ami Prefecture, and relieved the siege of Hexi County.
translations.idiomatic: Lin'an Hui rebels besieged the prefectural seat; his troops drove them off, defeated them at Ami, and lifted the siege of Hexi.

sentences.zh: 是年冬，以病乞罷，因子春傑官雁平道，就養山西。

translations.literal: That winter, on grounds of illness he requested dismissal; because his son Chunjie held office on the Yanping circuit he went to Shanxi to receive his support.
translations.idiomatic: That winter he resigned for illness and retired to Shanxi where his son Chunjie served on the Yanping circuit.

sentences.zh: 同治元年，命會同巡撫英桂防河，尋命赴陝西會辦軍務。

translations.literal: In the first year of the Tongzhi reign he was ordered to join Governor Yinggui in guarding the Yellow River, and soon was ordered to go to Shaanxi to jointly manage military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In Tongzhi 1 he joined Governor Yinggui on river defense, then was sent to Shaanxi for joint military affairs.

sentences.zh: 十年，卒，詔依例賜卹。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he died; an edict granted condolence payments according to precedent.
translations.idiomatic: He died in year 10; the court granted the usual mourning stipend.

sentences.zh: =張亮基=張亮基，字石卿，江蘇銅山人。

translations.literal: Zhang Liangji, style name Shiqing, was a native of Tongshan in Jiangsu.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Liangji, style Shiqing, was from Tongshan in Jiangsu.

sentences.zh: 道光十四年舉人，入貲為內閣中書。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year of the Daoguang reign he passed the provincial examination; he purchased office as a secretary in the Grand Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: A provincial graduate in Daoguang 14, he bought appointment as Grand Secretariat secretary.

sentences.zh: 從大學士王鼎赴河南治河，督築西壩。

translations.literal: He followed Grand Secretary Wang Ding to Henan to manage the river works and supervised construction of the western embankment.
translations.idiomatic: He accompanied Grand Secretary Wang Ding to Henan for river works and oversaw the western embankment.

sentences.zh: 工竣，賜花翎，擢侍讀。

translations.literal: When the work was completed he was granted the peacock feather insignia and promoted to reader.
translations.idiomatic: On completion he received the peacock feather and promotion to reader.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，出為雲南臨安知府，總督林則徐曾與共事河工，知其才，密薦可大用，調署永昌。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year he went out as prefect of Lin'an in Yunnan; Governor-General Lin Zexu had worked with him on river projects, knew his talent, secretly recommended him as fit for great employment, and transferred him to act at Yongchang.
translations.idiomatic: In year 26 he became Lin'an prefect in Yunnan; Lin Zexu, who knew his ability from river work, secretly recommended him and had him act at Yongchang.

sentences.zh: 邊夷滋擾，亮基用土弁左大雄擒匪首，事乃定。

translations.literal: Border tribes grew troublesome; Liangji used the native officer Zuo Daxiong to capture the bandit chief, and the affair was then settled.
translations.idiomatic: When border tribes stirred, Liangji had native officer Zuo Daxiong seize the rebel chief and restore calm.

sentences.zh: 超擢雲南按察使，就遷布政使。

translations.literal: He was promoted beyond the regular sequence to Yunnan provincial judicial commissioner and then moved directly to provincial administration commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He was fast-tracked to judicial commissioner and then administration commissioner of Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 三十年，擢雲南巡撫，兼署雲貴總督。

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year he was promoted to governor of Yunnan and concurrently acted as governor-general of Yunnan and Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In year 30 he became Yunnan governor and acting Yunnan-Guizhou governor-general.

sentences.zh: 粵匪漸熾，嘗密疏論軍事，文宗韙之。

translations.literal: As Cantonese rebels grew fiercer he once sent a secret memorial discussing military affairs, which the Wenzong Emperor approved.
translations.idiomatic: As Cantonese rebellion intensified he sent secret military memorials that Emperor Wenzong endorsed.

sentences.zh: 咸豐二年，調湖南巡撫，在途聞賊圍長沙，疏請駐守常德。

translations.literal: In the second year of the Xianfeng reign he was transferred to governor of Hunan; on the road he heard that bandits besieged Changsha and memorialized to garrison at Changde.
translations.idiomatic: Transferred to Hunan in Xianfeng 2, he learned en route that rebels besieged Changsha and asked to hold Changde.

sentences.zh: 詔趣進解省城之圍，至則梯城而入，屢出隊與城外援軍夾擊，賊解圍去。

translations.literal: An edict urged him to advance quickly to relieve the siege of the provincial capital; when he arrived he entered by scaling ladders on the wall, repeatedly led sorties to strike jointly with external relief troops, and the bandits lifted the siege and departed.
translations.idiomatic: Ordered to relieve the capital, he scaled the walls, sallied repeatedly with outside relief, and broke the siege.

sentences.zh: 破岳州，入湖北，漢陽、武昌相繼陷，湖廣總督徐廣縉以罪罷，命亮基代之，規進剿。

translations.literal: They broke Yuezhou and entered Hubei; Hanyang and Wuchang fell in succession; Huguang governor-general Xu Guangjin was dismissed for crime, and Liangji was ordered to replace him and plan advance suppression.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels took Yuezhou and swept into Hubei; Hanyang and Wuchang fell; Xu Guangjin was dismissed and Liangji ordered to replace him for a counteroffensive.

sentences.zh: 亮基疏言宜防賊回竄，意在專顧湖南，詔趣速進。

translations.literal: Liangji memorialized that one should guard against the bandits' return south; his intent was to focus on Hunan alone; an edict urged rapid advance.
translations.idiomatic: Liangji urged guarding against a southern return—really to keep focus on Hunan—until the throne ordered him forward.

sentences.zh: 三年春，賊棄武漢東下，亮基抵湖北籌辦收復撫卹事宜。

translations.literal: In the spring of the third year the bandits abandoned Wuhan and went east; Liangji reached Hubei to arrange recovery and consolation.
translations.idiomatic: In spring of year 3 rebels abandoned Wuhan for the east; Liangji reached Hubei to organize recovery and relief.

sentences.zh: 通城、崇陽、嘉魚、廣濟土匪起，平之。

translations.literal: Bandits rose in Tongcheng, Chongyang, Jiayu, and Guangji; he pacified them.
translations.idiomatic: He suppressed local bandits in Tongcheng, Chongyang, Jiayu, and Guangji.

sentences.zh: 賊自下游分竄江西，亮基督師扼道士洑、黃石港，分兵赴援。

translations.literal: Bandits from the lower reaches split into Jiangxi; Liangji personally led the army to hold Daoshifu and Huangshigang and divided troops to go to their aid.
translations.idiomatic: When downstream rebels split toward Jiangxi, Liangji held Daoshifu and Huangshigang and sent detachments to assist.

sentences.zh: 秋，賊之分竄河南者，由羅山入湖北黃安、麻城境，水陸夾擊，殲之。

translations.literal: In autumn the bandits who had split into Henan entered the territory of Huang'an and Macheng in Hubei by way of Luoshan; he struck them by land and water and annihilated them.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn Henan-bound raiders entered Huang'an and Macheng via Luoshan; he destroyed them in combined land-and-water attacks.

sentences.zh: 調山東巡撫，未行，江西賊由九江來犯，令道員徐豐玉御之於田家鎮，戰失利，豐玉陣亡，亮基坐降四級留任。

translations.literal: He was transferred to governor of Shandong; before he took up the post, Jiangxi bandits came from Jiujiang to attack; he ordered Circuit Intendant Xu Fengyu to resist them at Tianjiazhen; the battle was lost, Fengyu died in battle, and Liangji was demoted four ranks but retained in office.
translations.idiomatic: Transferred to Shandong, he was still en route when Jiujiang rebels struck; Intendant Xu Fengyu died at Tianjiazhen in defeat and Liangji was demoted four ranks but kept his post.

sentences.zh: 時粵匪李開芳等犯畿輔，踞靜海。

translations.literal: At that time Cantonese rebels Li Kaifang and others invaded the capital region and occupied Jinghai.
translations.idiomatic: Cantonese rebels led by Li Kaifang meanwhile invaded the capital approaches and held Jinghai.

sentences.zh: 亮基至山東，奉命扼德州，防其南逸。

translations.literal: Liangji reached Shandong and was ordered to hold Dezhou and block their escape south.
translations.idiomatic: Reaching Shandong, he was told to hold Dezhou against a southern breakout.

sentences.zh: 南路賊欲由淮、徐窺伺北犯為應援，令按察使厲恩官率兵駐宿遷之北以防之。

translations.literal: Southern-route bandits wished to spy northward through Huai and Xu as support for a northern thrust; he ordered Provincial Judicial Commissioner Li En'guan to lead troops to camp north of Suqian to guard against them.
translations.idiomatic: Expecting a Huai-Xu probe to support the northern drive, he posted Li En'guan north of Suqian.

sentences.zh: 四年，賊入山東境，亮基馳扼濟寧，杜其北竄。

translations.literal: In the fourth year bandits entered Shandong territory; Liangji hurried to hold Jining and block their escape north.
translations.idiomatic: In year 4 rebels entered Shandong; he rushed to Jining to block a northern escape.

sentences.zh: 尋陷鄆城，擾範縣、壽張、東平，繞出賊前截擊，敗之於臨清黑家莊。

translations.literal: Soon they took Yuncheng and harassed Fan County, Shouzhang, and Dongping; he circled ahead of the bandits to intercept and defeated them at Heijiazhuang in Linqing.
translations.idiomatic: They seized Yuncheng and raided Fan, Shouzhang, and Dongping; he cut ahead and routed them at Heijiazhuang near Linqing.

sentences.zh: 既奏捷，幫辦軍務大臣勝保劾其取巧冒功，詔斥亮基欺罔，並追論初赴湖南不急趨長沙，及去湖北時但求自全，居心狡詐，職，遣戍軍台。

translations.literal: After he had reported victory, Grand Minister for Suppression Sheng Bao impeached him for seizing cleverness and claiming merit falsely; an edict rebuked Liangji for deception, and also reviewed his initial journey to Hunan without hurrying to Changsha and his leaving Hubei while only seeking self-preservation, with crafty intent, stripped him of office, and sent him to exile at the military garrison.
translations.idiomatic: After his victory report, Sheng Bao accused him of fraud; the throne called Liangji deceitful, cited his slow march to Changsha and self-preserving exit from Hubei, stripped his rank, and exiled him to the garrison posts.

sentences.zh: 逾年，給事中毛鴻賓言臨清之役，勝保妄劾，御史宗稷辰亦言亮基能任事，未盡其用，乃釋回，發東河差遣，尋命往安徽隨辦軍務。

translations.literal: After more than a year, Supervising Secretary Mao Hongbin said that in the Linqing campaign Sheng Bao had impeached falsely, and Censor Zong Jichen also said Liangji was capable of affairs and had not been fully used; he was then released and returned, assigned to the Eastern River post, and soon ordered to go to Anhui to follow in managing military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: A year later Mao Hongbin showed Sheng Bao's charge at Linqing was false; Censor Zong Jichen argued Liangji was underused; he was recalled, sent to Eastern River duty, then Anhui military affairs.

sentences.zh: 七年，予五品頂戴，命赴雲南幫辦剿匪事宜。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was given the fifth-rank official cap and ordered to go to Yunnan to assist in suppressing bandit affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In year 7 he received fifth-rank cap rank and orders to Yunnan to help suppress rebels.

sentences.zh: 雲南迴匪方熾，團練橫行省會，總督吳振棫初至，駐曲靖，裁抑練勇，招撫回眾。

translations.literal: Yunnan Hui bandits were then fierce; militia ran rampant in the provincial capital; Governor-General Wu Zhenyu had just arrived and was encamped at Qujing, cutting back militia and recruiting pacification of Hui masses.
translations.idiomatic: Yunnan Hui rebellion raged and capital militia ruled the streets; Wu Zhenyu, newly arrived at Qujing, was curbing militia and wooing Hui submission.

sentences.zh: 霑益回最悍，集眾犯宣威，亮基督按察使徐之銘等率兵擊走之。

translations.literal: The Zhanyi Hui were fiercest; gathering a host they attacked Xuanwei; Liangji ordered Provincial Judicial Commissioner Xu Zhiming and others to lead troops and drive them off.
translations.idiomatic: The fiercest Zhanyi Hui gathered to strike Xuanwei; Liangji had Xu Zhiming and others repulse them.

sentences.zh: 八年春，又敗之於袁家屯，殲賊甚眾，餘黨就撫，詔嘉之，授雲南巡撫。

translations.literal: In the spring of the eighth year he again defeated them at Yuanjiatun, destroyed many bandits, and the remainder submitted to pacification; an edict praised him and he was appointed governor of Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: In spring of year 8 he routed them at Yuanjiatun, killed many, and accepted the rest; the court praised him and made him Yunnan governor.

sentences.zh: 既而振棫乞罷，擢雲貴總督，亮基薦徐之銘代為巡撫。

translations.literal: Soon after Zhenyu requested dismissal; he was promoted to governor-general of Yunnan and Guizhou, and Liangji recommended Xu Zhiming to replace him as governor.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhenyu resigned, Wu became governor-general and Liangji recommended Xu Zhiming as governor.

sentences.zh: 臨安回匪攻城，擾及阿迷，剿平之。

translations.literal: Hui bandits in Lin'an attacked the city and disturbed Ami as well; he suppressed and pacified them.
translations.idiomatic: Lin'an Hui besieged the city and threatened Ami; he suppressed them.

sentences.zh: 九年，省回就撫後，踞碧雞關，劫奪近郊，分剿乃散。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, after provincial Hui had submitted to pacification, they occupied Biji Pass and plundered the near suburbs; only after divided suppression did they scatter.
translations.idiomatic: In year 9 pacified capital Hui seized Biji Pass and raided suburbs until dispersed by divided attacks.

sentences.zh: 又剿平彝、安寧、緬寧、楚雄諸匪，武定、羅次、富民、祿豐、祿勸諸州縣先後克復。

translations.literal: He also suppressed bandits in Yi, Anning, Mianning, and Chuxiong, and the prefectures and counties of Wuding, Luoci, Fumin, Lufeng, and Luquan were recovered in succession.
translations.idiomatic: He also cleared rebels in Yi, Anning, Mianning, and Chuxiong and recovered Wuding, Luoci, Fumin, Lufeng, and Luquan.

sentences.zh: 然回、練互相猜忌，亂機時起。

translations.literal: Yet Hui and militia mutually suspected one another, and the seeds of disorder arose from time to time.
translations.idiomatic: Still, Hui and militia distrusted each other and unrest flickered on.

sentences.zh: 徐之銘既為巡撫，貪縱險狠，與亮基陰不相能，時構煽其間。

translations.literal: Once Xu Zhiming became governor he was greedy, unrestrained, fierce, and cruel; he and Liangji were secretly incompatible and constantly stirred trouble between them.
translations.idiomatic: Governor Xu Zhiming proved greedy, brutal, and secretly hostile, constantly stirring trouble against Liangji.

sentences.zh: 十年秋，回人掌教馬德新、徐元吉，武生馬現，率各屬回民來省乞撫，住城外江右館，亮基約之銘同詣撫諭。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the tenth year Hui religious teacher Ma Dexin, Xu Yuanji, and military licentiate Ma Xian led Hui people of various districts to the province to beg pacification, lodging outside the city at the Jiangyou Lodge; Liangji invited Zhiming to go together to pacify and instruct them.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn of year 10 Ma Dexin, Xu Yuanji, and Ma Xian led district Hui to beg pacification, lodging at the Jiangyou hostel outside the walls; Liangji asked Xu Zhiming to join him in parley.

sentences.zh: 之銘陰嗾已散練丁擁至督署阻撓，諭之不可，殺通海知縣雷焱於門，遂逼殺招撫委員紳士馬椿齡、孫鈞。

translations.literal: Zhiming secretly incited already dispersed militiamen to crowd to the governor's office to obstruct; instruction availed nothing; he killed Tonghai magistrate Lei Yan at the gate, and then compelled the killing of pacification commissioners and gentry Ma Chunling and Sun Jun.
translations.idiomatic: Xu secretly rallied disbanded militia to block the governor's yamen; when persuasion failed they killed Tonghai magistrate Lei Yan at the gate and forced the murder of pacification commissioners Ma Chunling and Sun Jun.

sentences.zh: 亮基為所脅持，不敢入告，以病乞罷，命劉源灝代之。

translations.literal: Liangji was coerced and dared not enter to report; he requested dismissal on grounds of illness, and Liu Yuanhao was ordered to replace him.
translations.idiomatic: Coerced, Liangji dared not report upward; he pleaded illness and Liu Yuanhao was named to succeed.

sentences.zh: 源灝久不至，亮基迳去。

translations.literal: Yuanhao long did not arrive; Liangji left directly.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanhao delayed; Liangji departed without waiting.

sentences.zh: 十一年，至湖北，乃疏陳滇事，劾之銘不法。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, reaching Hubei, he then memorialized stating Yunnan affairs and impeached Zhiming's lawlessness.
translations.idiomatic: In year 11, reaching Hubei, he memorialized on Yunnan and impeached Xu's crimes.

sentences.zh: 會布政使鄧爾恆升任陝西巡撫，去滇，之銘嗾匪戕於路。

translations.literal: At the time Provincial Administration Commissioner Deng Erheng was promoted to governor of Shaanxi and left Yunnan; Zhiming incited bandits to kill him on the road.
translations.idiomatic: As Administration Commissioner Deng Erheng left for Shaanxi governor, Xu incited rebels to murder him on the road.

sentences.zh: 於是罷源灝，以潘鐸署總督，命亮基赴滇查辦，督師剿匪。

translations.literal: Thereupon Yuanhao was dismissed; Pan Duo was appointed acting governor-general; Liangji was ordered to go to Yunnan to investigate and handle affairs and command troops to suppress bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanhao was removed, Pan Duo named acting governor-general, and Liangji ordered to Yunnan to investigate and command suppression.

sentences.zh: 亮基疏請發部照募損充餉，募勇千人然後行，與潘鐸先後至四川，欲資其餉力、兵力。

translations.literal: Liangji memorialized requesting issuance of ministry credentials to recruit by purchase to fill funds, to recruit one thousand braves and then depart; he and Pan Duo reached Sichuan in succession, wishing to draw on its funds and military strength.
translations.idiomatic: Liangji asked for ministry licenses to raise funds by sale of office, to recruit a thousand men before marching; he and Pan Duo reached Sichuan hoping for money and troops.

sentences.zh: 四川兵事未定，無以濟之。

translations.literal: Sichuan's military affairs were not settled, and there was nothing with which to aid them.
translations.idiomatic: Sichuan itself was still at war and could offer no help.

sentences.zh: 林自清者，亮基之舊部，方署雲南提督，與之銘及馬如龍等皆不協，回人仇之。

translations.literal: Lin Ziqing was Liangji's old subordinate, then acting Yunnan provincial military commissioner; he was at odds with Zhiming and Ma Rulong and others, and Hui people hated him.
translations.idiomatic: Liangji's former subordinate Lin Ziqing, acting Yunnan commander, clashed with Xu Zhiming and Ma Rulong and was hated by the Hui.

sentences.zh: 聞亮基在四川，擅率所部號萬人入川求效用，阻之不聽。

translations.literal: Hearing Liangji was in Sichuan, he on his own authority led his command, said to number ten thousand, into Sichuan to seek employment; they blocked him but he would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Learning Liangji was in Sichuan, Lin marched ten thousand men into the province on his own authority; orders to stop him failed.

sentences.zh: 詔亮基撫諭解散，而之銘嗾馬如龍等聲言拒亮基不使入境，相持久之。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Liangji to pacify and instruct them to disband, but Zhiming incited Ma Rulong and others to proclaim refusal to let Liangji enter the border, and the stalemate dragged on.
translations.idiomatic: The throne told Liangji to disband them, while Xu incited Ma Rulong to bar Liangji from Yunnan, prolonging the impasse.

sentences.zh: 同治元年，潘鐸先抵任，請暫留之銘以畢撫局，遂改命亮基以總督銜署貴州巡撫。

translations.literal: In the first year of the Tongzhi reign Pan Duo first reached his post and requested to retain Zhiming temporarily to complete the pacification situation; Liangji was then reassigned with governor-general rank to act as governor of Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In Tongzhi 1 Pan Duo arrived and asked to keep Xu Zhiming to finish pacification; Liangji was instead named acting Guizhou governor with governor-general rank.

sentences.zh: 未幾，之銘复陰嗾回眾​​為變，鐸被戕，而雲南之亂愈亟矣。

translations.literal: Before long Zhiming again secretly incited Hui masses to revolt; Pan was killed, and Yunnan's disorder grew more urgent still.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Xu again stirred Hui rebellion; Pan Duo was murdered and Yunnan collapsed further.

sentences.zh: 二年，亮基至貴州，黃號、白號、苗、教諸匪並熾，上下游遍地皆賊。

translations.literal: In the second year Liangji reached Guizhou; Yellow Banner, White Banner, Miao, and sect bandits were all fierce, and up and down the river bandits were everywhere.
translations.idiomatic: In year 2 he reached Guizhou to find Yellow and White Banner rebels, Miao, and sectarians raging along every reach of the river.

sentences.zh: 亮基令總兵沈宏富等攻遵義螺螄堰，破之，殲餘匪於上稽場。

translations.literal: Liangji ordered Regional Commander Shen Hongfu and others to attack the Luosi weir at Zunyi, broke it, and annihilated remnant bandits at Shangji field.
translations.idiomatic: He had Shen Hongfu break the Luosi weir at Zunyi and wipe out survivors at Shangji.

sentences.zh: 令總兵劉義方等剿思南教匪，复普安、安南，又連破苗匪於桐梓鼎城及水城廳馬龍胯，擒匪首何潤科等於黔西，降萬人。

translations.literal: He ordered Regional Commander Liu Yifang and others to suppress sect bandits in Sinan, recovered Pu'an and Annan, and again repeatedly defeated Miao bandits at Dingcheng in Tongzi and Malongkua in Shuicheng Department, capturing bandit chiefs He Runke and others in western Guizhou and accepting the surrender of ten thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yifang crushed Sinan sectarians, retook Pu'an and Annan, defeated Miao at Tongzi and Shuicheng, captured He Runke in western Guizhou, and accepted ten thousand surrenders.

sentences.zh: 三年，尚大坪匪犯省城，督沈宏富等戰於郊，殲賊千計，復修文。

translations.literal: In the third year Shangdaping bandits attacked the provincial capital; he supervised Shen Hongfu and others in battle in the suburbs, destroyed more than a thousand bandits, and recovered Xiuwen.
translations.idiomatic: In year 3 Shangdaping rebels threatened the capital; suburban fighting killed thousands and Xiuwen was recovered.

sentences.zh: 總兵林自清、趙德昌克龍里，又復興義，解清鎮之圍，收復定番、廣順、長寨諸城，破龍泉、湄潭黃、白號匪老巢，克滇西衛城。

translations.literal: Regional Commanders Lin Ziqing and Zhao Dechang took Longli, again recovered Xingyi, relieved the siege of Qingzhen, recovered the cities of Dingfan, Guangshun, and Changzhai, broke the old lairs of Yellow and White Banner bandits in Longquan and Meitan, and took the Weicheng of western Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: Lin Ziqing and Zhao Dechang took Longli, relieved Xingyi and Qingzhen, recovered Dingfan, Guangshun, and Changzhai, destroyed Longquan-Meitan sect lairs, and seized western Yunnan's Weicheng.

sentences.zh: 四年，克黔西石阡、永寧、荔波，貴州地瘠財匱，飢軍索餉，時虞譁噪。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he took Shiqian and Yongning in western Guizhou and Libo; Guizhou's land was poor and funds scarce, hungry soldiers demanded pay, and mutiny was feared from time to time.
translations.idiomatic: In year 4 he took Shiqian, Yongning, and Libo while starving troops in impoverished Guizhou clamored for pay.

sentences.zh: 亮基撫馭防剿，僅得粗安，而所部諸將多驕蹇，輿論不協，為侍讀學士景其濬論劾。

translations.literal: Liangji pacified and guarded against suppression and obtained only rough peace, but the generals under him were mostly arrogant and obstinate, public opinion was not in harmony, and Hanlin Reader Jing Qijun memorialized in impeachment.
translations.idiomatic: Liangji barely kept order while his generals grew insubordinate; Reader Jing Qijun impeached him.

sentences.zh: 亮基乃劾總兵林自清、劉有勳，副將池有連等劫掠扣餉，不聽調度，請嚴治。

translations.literal: Liangji then impeached Regional Commander Lin Ziqing and Liu Youxun, Vice Commander Chi Youlian and others for plundering and withholding pay and not obeying command, requesting severe punishment.
translations.idiomatic: He counter-impeached Lin Ziqing, Liu Youxun, and Chi Youlian for looting, withholding pay, and disobedience.

sentences.zh: 詔布政使嚴樹森察奏，亮基復具疏自陳，言樹森規避貴州，安坐鄰省不親至，於是亮基、樹森並褫職。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Provincial Administration Commissioner Yan Shusen to investigate and report; Liangji again submitted a memorial stating his own case, saying Shusen evaded Guizhou and sat at ease in a neighboring province without coming in person; thereupon Liangji and Shusen were both stripped of office.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Shusen was ordered to investigate; Liangji accused Yan of avoiding Guizhou from a neighboring province—both men were dismissed.

sentences.zh: 十年，卒。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in year 10.

sentences.zh: 湖南巡撫王文韶、貴州巡撫曾璧光先後請復原銜，各建專祠。

translations.literal: Hunan Governor Wang Wenshao and Guizhou Governor Zeng Biguang successively requested restoration of his original rank; each province built a dedicated shrine.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Wenshao of Hunan and Zeng Biguang of Guizhou later secured restoration of his rank and local shrines.

sentences.zh: 光緒三十四年，湖南、貴州京官合詞臚陳功德在民，追諡惠肅。

translations.literal: In the thirty-fourth year of the Guangxu reign Hunan and Guizhou capital officials jointly memorialized listing his merit among the people, and he was posthumously given the temple name Huisu.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangxu 34 capital officials from Hunan and Guizhou petitioned for his merits; he received the posthumous name Huisu.

sentences.zh: =毛鴻賓=毛鴻賓，字翊雲，山東歷城人。

translations.literal: Mao Hongbin, style name Yiyun, was a native of Licheng in Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: Mao Hongbin, style Yiyun, came from Licheng in Shandong.

sentences.zh: 道光十八年進士，選庶吉士，授編修。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year of the Daoguang reign he passed the jinshi examination, was selected as a bachelor in the Hanlin Academy, and was appointed reviser.
translations.idiomatic: He became a jinshi in Daoguang 18, entered the Hanlin, and was appointed reviser.

sentences.zh: 遷御史、給事中，數上封事論軍務。

translations.literal: He was transferred to censor and supervising secretary and several times submitted sealed memorials discussing military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to censor and supervising secretary and repeatedly memorialized on military affairs.

sentences.zh: 咸豐三年，以尚書孫瑞珍薦，命回籍治團練。

translations.literal: In the third year of the Xianfeng reign, on the recommendation of Minister Sun Ruizhen, he was ordered to return to his native place to organize militia.
translations.idiomatic: In Xianfeng 3, on Sun Ruizhen's recommendation, he was sent home to organize militia.

sentences.zh: 四年，劾幫辦軍務大臣勝保罪狀，請嚴旨查辦。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he impeached the crimes of Grand Minister for Suppression Sheng Bao and requested a stern edict for investigation and handling.
translations.idiomatic: In year 4 he impeached Sheng Bao and demanded a stern imperial inquiry.

sentences.zh: 五年，授湖北荊宜施道，調安襄鄖荊道，歷安徽按察使、江蘇布政使。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was appointed Jing-Yi-Shi circuit intendant in Hubei, transferred to An-Xiang-Yun-Jing circuit intendant, and successively served as Anhui provincial judicial commissioner and Jiangsu provincial administration commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In year 5 he took Hubei and Anxiang circuit posts, then Anhui judicial commissioner and Jiangsu administration commissioner.

sentences.zh: 十一年，署湖南巡撫，尋實授。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he acted as governor of Hunan and soon received substantive appointment.
translations.idiomatic: In year 11 he acted as Hunan governor, then received full appointment.

sentences.zh: 疏言：「湖南地居僻遠，向非富強，自前撫臣張亮基、駱秉章等於吏治民風實力講求，用能削平寇盜，屹為上游重鎮，用人之效，有明徵矣。

translations.literal: In a memorial he said: 'Hunan lies in a remote place and was never rich or strong; since former governors Zhang Liangji, Luo Bingzhang, and others earnestly pursued administration and local custom, they were able to cut down bandits and stand firm as a vital upstream stronghold—the effect of employing men has clear proof.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote: 'Hunan was never naturally strong; under Zhang Liangji and Luo Bingzhang it became an upstream bastion through real attention to governance—proof that good appointments matter.

sentences.zh: 臣以為名將不過收戰陣之功，得賢督撫，斯能造封疆之福。

translations.literal: Your servant considers that famous generals can collect no more than battlefield merit; obtain worthy governors and they can create the fortune of a frontier.
translations.idiomatic: Famous generals win battles; worthy governors secure whole frontiers.

sentences.zh: 如左宗棠識略過人，其才力不在曾國籓、胡林翼之下，今但使之帶勇，殊不足以盡其長，倘畀以封疆重任，必能保境安民，兼顧大局。

translations.literal: Such as Zuo Zongtang, whose strategic insight surpasses others—his talent and strength are not below Zeng Guofan and Hu Linyi; now if he is only made to lead braves, that is truly insufficient to exhaust his strengths; if entrusted with a heavy frontier responsibility, he will surely be able to guard the territory and settle the people and also attend to the overall situation.
translations.idiomatic: Zuo Zongtang rivals Zeng Guofan and Hu Linyi; leading troops alone wastes his gifts—a frontier post would let him guard the realm and serve the larger strategy.

sentences.zh: 前任雲貴總督張亮基，果決有為，雲南壤接邊陲，餉糈不給，漢、回仇釁相尋，即令經營盡善，亦僅有益一隅，似不若任以要地，俾展所長。

translations.literal: The former Yunnan-Guizhou governor-general Zhang Liangji is resolute and capable; Yunnan's soil borders the frontier, funds and grain are not supplied, Han and Hui vendettas follow one another—even if managed to perfection it would only benefit one corner; it seems better to assign him a vital post and let him display his strengths.
translations.idiomatic: Former governor-general Zhang Liangji is decisive, yet Yunnan's border troubles and Han-Hui strife limit him to local effect; a key inland post would better use his talents.

sentences.zh: 但使東南日有轉機，則云、貴遊氛無難迅掃，此輕重之機宜審者也。

translations.literal: If only the southeast daily gains a turning point, then the roaming unrest of Yunnan and Guizhou will not be hard to sweep away swiftly; this is a matter in which the weight of priorities must be carefully weighed.
translations.idiomatic: Once the southeast stabilizes, Yunnan and Guizhou will follow—that is how priorities should be weighed.'

sentences.zh: 」時湘軍所至有功，各省多往召募，鴻賓疏陳招勇流弊，請慎選將領以收實效，並被嘉納。

translations.literal: ' At that time wherever the Hunan Army went there was achievement, and many provinces went to recruit them; Hongbin memorialized stating the abuses of recruiting braves and requested careful selection of generals to obtain real effect, and this too was praised and accepted.
translations.idiomatic: As Hunan armies succeeded, provinces rushed to recruit; Hongbin warned of recruitment abuses and urged choosing capable commanders—the court approved.

sentences.zh: 石達開竄湖南，鴻賓遣知府席寶田、副將周達武、總兵趙福元分路進擊，解會同、黔陽之圍。

translations.literal: Shi Dakai fled into Hunan; Hongbin sent Prefect Xi Baotian, Vice Commander Zhou Dawu, and Regional Commander Zhao Fuyuan to advance by separate routes and strike, relieving the sieges of Huitong and Qianyang.
translations.idiomatic: When Shi Dakai entered Hunan, Hongbin sent Xi Baotian, Zhou Dawu, and Zhao Fuyuan by separate routes to lift sieges at Huitong and Qianyang.

sentences.zh: 同治元年，進復來鳳，貴州提督田興恕兼署巡撫，軍報不實，信用左右，鴻賓疏劾之。

translations.literal: In the first year of the Tongzhi reign he advanced and recovered Laifeng; Guizhou Provincial Military Commissioner Tian Xingyu concurrently acted as governor, military reports were untrue, and he trusted his close attendants; Hongbin memorialized in impeachment.
translations.idiomatic: In Tongzhi 1 he retook Laifeng and impeached Guizhou commander Tian Xingyu, acting governor, for false reports and favoritism.

sentences.zh: 遣兵越境剿貴州竄匪，复天柱縣城。

translations.literal: He sent troops across the border to suppress Guizhou raiding bandits and recovered Tiancheng County seat.
translations.idiomatic: He crossed into Guizhou to chase raiders and recovered Tiancheng.

sentences.zh: 又剿銅仁張家寨，匪首蕭文魁率眾降，克大小青兩堡。

translations.literal: He again suppressed Zhang Family Stockade in Tongren; bandit chief Xiao Wenkui led the masses to surrender, and he took the great and small Qing forts.
translations.idiomatic: At Tongren's Zhang Family Stockade, Xiao Wenkui surrendered and both Qing forts fell.

sentences.zh: 江藍廳同知椿齡指團紳為土匪，鴻賓廉知椿齡有酷刑逼借事，劾罷之。

translations.literal: Tongling, subprefectural magistrate of Jianglan Department, accused militia gentry of being bandits; Hongbin on investigation knew Tongling had used cruel torture to force loans and impeached and dismissed him.
translations.idiomatic: Jianglan subprefect Tongling called militia leaders bandits; Hongbin found he had tortured men to extort loans and removed him.

sentences.zh: 椿齡京控，訐鴻賓借貸不遂，鴻賓自請查辦，下總督官文鞫訊，得白。

translations.literal: Tongling appealed in the capital, accusing Hongbin of failing to obtain a loan; Hongbin requested investigation on his own initiative; the case was sent to Governor-General Guan Wen for examination, and he was cleared.
translations.idiomatic: Tongling appealed in Beijing that Hongbin had denied him a loan; Hongbin asked for inquiry and was exonerated by Guan Wen.

sentences.zh: 擢兩廣總督，英德土匪起，令按察使張運蘭剿平之。

translations.literal: He was promoted to governor-general of Guangdong and Guangxi; bandits rose in Yingde, and he ordered Provincial Judicial Commissioner Zhang Yunlan to suppress and pacify them.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to Guangdong-Guangxi governor-general, he had Zhang Yunlan suppress Yingde bandits.

sentences.zh: 偕巡撫郭嵩燾奏定變通緝捕章程，獲大盜者予優擢，允之。

translations.literal: Together with Governor Guo Songtao he memorialized to fix flexible arrest regulations, granting preferential promotion to those who captured great robbers, which was approved.
translations.idiomatic: With Governor Guo Songtao he secured approval for flexible arrest rules rewarding capture of major bandits with promotion.

sentences.zh: 三年，江南既复，浙、贛餘氛未靖。

translations.literal: In the third year, once Jiangnan had been recovered, remnant unrest in Zhejiang and Jiangxi was not yet settled.
translations.idiomatic: In year 3, though Jiangnan was recovered, Zhejiang and Jiangxi still smoldered.

sentences.zh: 鴻賓疏言：「江西南路之防猶有未備，閩、粵交界均無防兵，慮賊上竄，以粵東為尾閭。

translations.literal: Hongbin memorialized: 'The defense of southern Jiangxi still has gaps unprepared; at the Fujian-Guangdong border there are no defensive troops on either side; I fear the bandits will thrust upward and take Guangdong east as their tail end.
translations.idiomatic: He warned: 'Southern Jiangxi remains weakly held; Fujian and Guangdong borders lack troops; rebels may drive north with Guangdong as their rear.

sentences.zh: 江西當四沖之地，宜合數省兵力，乘大勝餘威，聚而殲之。

translations.literal: Jiangxi stands at a place of four crossings; it is fitting to combine the military strength of several provinces, ride the momentum of great victory, gather and annihilate them.
translations.idiomatic: Jiangxi is a crossroads—several provinces should combine forces while victory is fresh and destroy them together.

sentences.zh: 已諮曾國籓調撥勁旅，繞越寧郡、石城一帶，扼賊南竄之路，臣派一軍於閩、粵交界會同進剿。

translations.literal: I have already consulted Zeng Guofan to transfer elite troops, bypassing Ning Prefecture and Shicheng and the like, to hold the bandits' southern escape route; your servant will dispatch one army at the Fujian-Guangdong border to join in advance suppression.
translations.idiomatic: He had asked Zeng Guofan for elite troops to block escape routes through Ning and Shicheng while he sent a column to the Fujian-Guangdong border.

sentences.zh: 並請敕曾國籓嚴守南贛，俾毋竄越。

translations.literal: And I request an edict to Zeng Guofan to strictly guard southern Ganzhou, so that they may not flee across.
translations.idiomatic: He also asked the throne to order Zeng to seal southern Ganzhou against breakout.'

sentences.zh: 四年，坐前在湖南，道員胡鏞請諮引見，繳回咨文，委署道缺，降一級調用，回籍。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was punished for a prior matter in Hunan when Circuit Intendant Hu Yong requested consultation for an audience, returned the consultation document, and appointed him to act in a circuit post; he was demoted one rank and transferred, and returned to his native place.
translations.idiomatic: In year 4 he was demoted one rank and sent home for mishandling Hunan intendant Hu Yong's audience request years earlier.

sentences.zh: 七年，卒。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in year 7.

sentences.zh: 宣統初，山東巡撫袁樹勳疏陳鴻賓功績，復原官，祀鄉賢祠。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Xuantong reign Shandong Governor Yuan Shuxun memorialized Hongbin's achievements; his original office was restored and he was enshrined in the local worthies' temple.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Xuantong, Shandong governor Yuan Shuxun restored his rank and enshrined him among local worthies.

sentences.zh: =張凱嵩=張凱嵩，字云卿，湖北江夏人。

translations.literal: Zhang Kaisong, style name Yunqing, was a native of Jiangxia in Hubei.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Kaisong, style Yunqing, was from Jiangxia in Hubei.

sentences.zh: 道光二十五年進士，廣西即用知縣，歷宣化、懷集、臨桂知縣。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year of the Daoguang reign he passed the jinshi examination, was appointed directly as magistrate in Guangxi, and successively served as magistrate of Xuanhua, Huaiji, and Lingui.
translations.idiomatic: A jinshi in Daoguang 25, he was posted directly as Guangxi magistrate at Xuanhua, Huaiji, and Lingui.

sentences.zh: 李星沅、勞崇光並薦其能，咸豐五年，擢慶遠知府。

translations.literal: Li Xingyuan and Luo Chongguang both recommended his ability; in the fifth year of the Xianfeng reign he was promoted to prefect of Qingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Recommended by Li Xingyuan and Luo Chongguang, he became Qingyuan prefect in Xianfeng 5.

sentences.zh: 剿平土匪王得勝等，擢左江道，調署右江道。

translations.literal: He suppressed and pacified bandits such as Wang Desheng and was promoted to Zuojiang circuit intendant and transferred to act as Youjiang circuit intendant.
translations.idiomatic: After suppressing Wang Desheng and other bandits he rose to Zuojiang intendant and acted at Youjiang.

sentences.zh: 慶遠失守，革職留任。

translations.literal: Qingyuan was lost; he was dismissed from office but retained in his post.
translations.idiomatic: When Qingyuan fell he was stripped of rank but kept on duty.

sentences.zh: 八年，偕按察使蔣益澧破賊，克慶遠，復原官，署按察使，尋實授，遷布政使。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, together with Provincial Judicial Commissioner Jiang Yili he defeated bandits, recovered Qingyuan, restored his original office, acted as provincial judicial commissioner, soon received substantive appointment, and was transferred to provincial administration commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In year 8 he and Jiang Yili retook Qingyuan, regained his rank, became judicial then administration commissioner.

sentences.zh: 同治元年，巡撫劉長佑赴潯州籌剿撫，留凱嵩經畫後路。

translations.literal: In the first year of the Tongzhi reign Governor Liu Changyou went to Xun Prefecture to plan suppression and pacification, leaving Kaisong to manage the rear route.
translations.idiomatic: In Tongzhi 1 Governor Liu Changyou went to Xunzhou for campaigns while Kaisong managed the rear.

sentences.zh: 荔浦張皋友陷陽朔，遣兵敗賊於鷓鴣岩，復其城，就擢巡撫。

translations.literal: Zhang Gaoyou of Lipu took Yangshuo; he sent troops to defeat bandits at Zhegu Rock and recover the city, and was thereupon promoted to governor.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Gaoyou seized Yangshuo, Kaisong routed him at Zhegu Rock, recovered the city, and was promoted governor.

sentences.zh: 諸匪中黃鼎鳳、張皋友最猖獗，分陷貴縣、陽朔、麕集大鹿灘、馬瀨，檄總兵李明惠、提督江忠義先剿馬瀨，進規貴縣，破之於桂嶺，殲擒賊首張皋友、陳土養。

translations.literal: Among the bandits Huang Dingfeng and Zhang Gaoyou were most rampant; they separately took Guixian, Yangshuo, Milu at Dalu Beach, and Mala; he ordered Regional Commander Li Minghui and Provincial Military Commissioner Jiang Zhongyi first to suppress Mala, advance on Guixian, broke them at Guiling, and destroyed and captured bandit chiefs Zhang Gaoyou and Chen Tuyang.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Dingfeng and Zhang Gaoyou were the worst, seizing Guixian, Yangshuo, Dalu Beach, and Mala; Li Minghui and Jiang Zhongyi crushed them at Guiling and captured Zhang and Chen Tuyang.

sentences.zh: 二年，檄布政使劉坤一攻黃鼎鳳於登龍橋。

translations.literal: In the second year he ordered Provincial Administration Commissioner Liu Kunyi to attack Huang Dingfeng at Denglong Bridge.
translations.idiomatic: In year 2 he sent Liu Kunyi against Huang Dingfeng at Denglong Bridge.

sentences.zh: 賊走覃塘，進圍之。

translations.literal: The bandits fled to Qintang and he advanced to besiege them.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels fled to Qintang and he pressed the siege.

sentences.zh: 信都賊陳金剛等來援，道員蔣澤春逆擊敗之，進克容縣，坤一克覃塘。

translations.literal: Xindu bandits Chen Jingang and others came to their aid; Circuit Intendant Jiang Zechun met and defeated them, advanced and took Rong County, and Kunyi took Qintang.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Jingang of Xindu marched to relieve them; Jiang Zechun defeated him, took Rong County, and Liu Kunyi took Qintang.

sentences.zh: 三年，克天平寨，擒黃鼎鳳。

translations.literal: In the third year he took Tianping Stockade and captured Huang Dingfeng.
translations.idiomatic: In year 3 Tianping Stockade fell and Huang Dingfeng was captured.

sentences.zh: 貴縣平，加頭品頂戴。

translations.literal: Guixian was pacified; he was given the first-rank official cap.
translations.idiomatic: With Guixian pacified he received the first-rank official cap.

sentences.zh: 疏陳左右江積匪未清，議三路進兵，以劉坤一統七營留防潯州，易元泰統十一營由賓州、遷江達思恩，李士恩統水陸八營由橫州達南寧，節節進剿。

translations.literal: In a memorial he stated that accumulated bandits of the Zuojiang and Youjiang had not been cleared and proposed advance by three routes: Liu Kunyi to command seven battalions remaining to guard Xun Prefecture, Yi Yuantai to command eleven battalions from Bin Prefecture and Qianjiang reaching Si'en, Li Shien to command eight land and water battalions from Heng Prefecture reaching Nanning, advancing step by step in suppression.
translations.idiomatic: He proposed a three-pronged campaign: Liu Kunyi holding Xunzhou, Yi Yuantai marching from Bin and Qianjiang toward Si'en, and Li Shien from Heng toward Nanning.

sentences.zh: 四年，坤一攻克大廟、江口、平菼，斬賊首梁安邦，南寧河道始通。

translations.literal: In the fourth year Kunyi took Damiao, Jiangkou, and Ping'an, beheaded bandit chief Liang Anbang, and the Nanning river route was finally open.
translations.idiomatic: In year 4 Liu Kunyi took Damiao, Jiangkou, and Ping'an, killed Liang Anbang, and opened the Nanning waterways.

sentences.zh: 元泰剿上林，平之。

translations.literal: Yuantai suppressed Shanglin and pacified it.
translations.idiomatic: Yi Yuantai pacified Shanglin.

sentences.zh: 坤一擢江西巡撫去，以同知劉培一代領其軍，將親赴南寧督戰，會偽康王汪海洋竄粵，將入廣西，詔凱嵩駐防潯州。

translations.literal: Kunyi was promoted to governor of Jiangxi and departed; Subprefectural Magistrate Liu Peiyi took command of his army in his place; he was about to go in person to Nanning to supervise battle when the false Prince of Kang Wang Wang Haiyang fled into Guangdong and was about to enter Guangxi; an edict ordered Kaisong to garrison at Xun Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Kunyi left for Jiangxi governor, Liu Peiyi took his troops, and Kaisong was ordered to hold Xunzhou when Wang Haiyang threatened Guangxi from Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 五年，凱嵩至南寧，進攻山澤，督諸軍穴地轟城，奪山入，擒偽平章蘇仲熙等。

translations.literal: In the fifth year Kaisong reached Nanning, advanced to attack Shanzhe, supervised the armies in tunneling to bombard the city, took the mountain and entered, and captured the false Pingzhang Su Zhongxi and others.
translations.idiomatic: In year 5 at Nanning he tunneled under Shanzhe, stormed the heights, and captured the rebel minister Su Zhongxi.

sentences.zh: 孫仁廣單騎走旺隴，追斬之。

translations.literal: Sun Renguang fled alone on horseback to Wanglong; he was pursued and beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Renguang fled alone toward Wanglong and was run down and killed.

sentences.zh: 山澤為賊所踞十餘年，至此悉平。

translations.literal: Shanzhe had been occupied by bandits for more than ten years; at this point it was entirely pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Shanzhe, held by rebels over ten years, was finally cleared.

sentences.zh: 六年，擢雲貴總督。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was promoted to governor-general of Yunnan and Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In year 6 he became Yunnan-Guizhou governor-general.

sentences.zh: 自潘鐸被戕，滇事益紛。

translations.literal: Since Pan Duo was killed, Yunnan affairs grew more tangled.
translations.idiomatic: After Pan Duo's murder Yunnan grew only more chaotic.

sentences.zh: 行至巴東，稱病，三疏請罷，坐規避，褫職。

translations.literal: Reaching Badong he claimed illness, three times memorialized to request dismissal, and was punished for evasion and stripped of office.
translations.idiomatic: At Badong he pleaded illness three times, was judged to be evading duty, and dismissed.

sentences.zh: 光緒六年，以五品京堂起用，授通政使參議，遷內閣侍讀學士，署順天府尹，授貴州巡撫。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of the Guangxu reign he was raised from fifth-rank Beijing official, appointed vice commissioner of the Office of Transmission, transferred to Hanlin reader in the Grand Secretariat, acted as Shuntian prefect, and was appointed governor of Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangxu 6 he reentered service as transmission vice commissioner, Hanlin reader, acting Shuntian prefect, then Guizhou governor.

sentences.zh: 十年，調雲南。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he was transferred to Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: In year 10 he was transferred to Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 請於省城設開採五金總局，以興礦利，偕內閣學士周德潤勘越南界務。

translations.literal: He requested establishment at the provincial capital of a general bureau for mining the five metals to develop mineral profit, and together with Hanlin Academician Zhou Derun surveyed Vietnam border affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He proposed a capital bureau for mining metals and joined Zhou Derun in surveying the Vietnam border.

sentences.zh: 十二年，卒於官。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office in year 12.

sentences.zh: 廣西巡撫李秉衡疏陳凱嵩政績，請建專祠，廣西京官論其不當，罷之。

translations.literal: Guangxi Governor Li Bingheng memorialized Kaisong's administrative achievements and requested a dedicated shrine; Guangxi capital officials argued it was inappropriate and it was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Li Bingheng sought a shrine for Kaisong, but Guangxi capital officials objected and the proposal was dropped.

sentences.zh: 子仲炘，光緒三年進士，由翰林御史官至通政司參議，敢言有聲。

translations.literal: His son Zhongxin passed the jinshi examination in the third year of the Guangxu reign; from Hanlin censor he rose to vice commissioner of the Office of Transmission, daring in speech and renowned.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhongxin, a Guangxu 3 jinshi, rose from Hanlin censor to transmission vice commissioner with a reputation for outspokenness.

sentences.zh: =【論】=論曰：雲南地居邊遠，回、漢積仇，中原多故之秋，幾為王靈所不及。

translations.literal: The commentary says: Yunnan lies in a remote border; Han and Hui bear accumulated hatred; in a season when the central plains had many troubles, it nearly fell beyond the reach of imperial authority.
translations.idiomatic: The commentators note: remote Yunnan, with Han-Hui vendettas amid central chaos, nearly slipped beyond imperial control.

sentences.zh: 吳振棫兼籌剿撫，實體中朝措置之難。

translations.literal: Wu Zhenyu jointly planned suppression and pacification, truly embodying the difficulty of the court's arrangements.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Zhenyu's combined pacification and suppression reflected how hard the court's task was.

sentences.zh: 張亮基才足有為，誤用徐之銘，受其排擠，遂至不可收拾。

translations.literal: Zhang Liangji's talent was sufficient for achievement, but he misused Xu Zhiming, suffered his exclusion, and thus reached a state beyond remedy.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Liangji was capable but erred in trusting Xu Zhiming, whose intrigues ruined what he had built.

sentences.zh: 自潘鐸被戕之後，無人敢任其艱危。

translations.literal: After Pan Duo was killed, no one dared undertake its peril.
translations.idiomatic: After Pan Duo's death none would face Yunnan's peril.

sentences.zh: 毛鴻賓疏言內地寇平，邊方自靖，誠為確論。

translations.literal: Mao Hongbin's memorial stating that when internal bandits are pacified the border will settle itself is indeed a sound judgment.
translations.idiomatic: Mao Hongbin was right that pacifying the interior would calm the frontier.

sentences.zh: 張凱嵩因規避黜，後仍以舊勞起用，朝廷固鑑其情已。

translations.literal: Zhang Kaisong was dismissed for evasion, yet later was raised again on account of old merit; the court had indeed discerned his circumstances.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Kaisong was dismissed for evasion yet later restored—the court had weighed his case fairly.
